title: Populated 0.7.0 database fixtures per driver
summary: Deterministic populated 0.7.0 databases exist for four scenarios (default storage, named storage, published core migration copies, schema-1 database) on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, can be restored later without 0.7.0 production code, and are asserted for full DDL, audit-table shape and row content.
why: I16 and I15 need real 0.7.0 data to prove in P3 that the split rewrites zero rows and that Audit adoption verifies the full audit_log shape. A fixture taken after any P2 change is not a 0.7.0 baseline, so it must be produced now from the unchanged code. Hard risk: persistence/data integrity on four drivers (name it in the report; Review P1.6 covers it).

include: tests/Fixtures/Baseline070/Persistence/Legacy070Schema.php: frozen test-side copy of the 0.7.0 DDL of AzGuard\Storage\Schema\StorageSchema (create of the seven 0.7.0 tables incl. audit_log, the schema-1 shape, and the schema-1 to schema-2 upgrade), so that restoring a fixture never calls production schema code that P3 changes
tests/Fixtures/Baseline070/Persistence/Dataset.php: one deterministic dataset written through the public 0.7.0 API (grant/revoke/sync/touch/expiry prune) on two panels sharing one storage

tests/Fixtures/Baseline070/Persistence/<driver>/<scenario>.json: canonical row dumps per driver (sqlite, pgsql, mysql, mariadb) and scenario (default, named, published, schema1) with a header {baseline, driver, scenario, generator, generated_at}
tests/Fixtures/Baseline070/Persistence/Restorer.php: rebuilds a scenario from Legacy070Schema plus raw inserts of a dump and records the migrations-table rows of that scenario

tests/Regression/Baseline070/PopulatedDatabaseTest.php: per current DB_CONNECTION and scenario — restore, compare DDL, audit_log shape, rows and migrations table; prove Legacy070Schema equals production 0.7.0 DDL
Scenario default: package-loaded core migrations 2026_10_01_000000_create_azguard_storage and 2026_10_09_000000_upgrade_azguard_storage_to_schema_2
Scenario named: a second storage installed through the application migration generated by azguard:storage:migration {name} (0.7.0 creates audit_log there through core)

Scenario published: core migrations published with vendor:publish --tag=azguard-migrations; both basenames identical to the package-loaded ones; the migrations table must show the published copies as already run

Scenario schema1: a schema version 1 storage (no subject_revisions, no panel_state.epoch, storage_state.schema version 1) populated before upgrade, then upgraded through the existing StorageSchema::upgrade path

Dataset content: permissions with metadata; role and permission grants that are global, tenant-wide (context_key = global), scoped (context_type/context_key set), with and without tenant, expired, NULL expiry, with actor fields, application grant columns and meta; panel_state, subject_revisions and storage_state rows; audit_log rows produced by the Audit plugin for every event type the dataset emits (unique event_id, payload with the 0.7.0 state keys)
exclude: Any change under packages/ (StorageSchema, migrations, installer, doctor, Audit plugin)
The Audit create-or-adopt migration and adoption logic (P3)
Fixtures for host_keys variants other than the default; the existing DdlSnapshot keeps covering uuid/bigint/ulid role_grants DDL

reads.why: Table ownership, migration identity, installation/upgrade scenarios and frozen formats the fixtures must make testable
I15 and I16 wording: what P3 will assert against these fixtures
Exact migration basenames, publish tags and generated-migration name patterns
0.7.0 DDL to freeze into Legacy070Schema (create, drop, upgrade, triggers, pair constraints)
Package-loaded/published migration body delegating to StorageSchema
Existing DDL capture (columns, indexes, check constraints, SQLite triggers) to reuse for shape comparison

reads.section: upgrades a schema 1 storage in place
reads.why: How the suite already reconstructs a schema-1 storage

rules: No production change: `git diff --quiet 09612160c98ca6133c894a8f90f5653b9dac6b8f -- packages/` must hold before generating and at hand-off.
Dumps are generated only from the unchanged 0.7.0 code, only in writer mode (`AZGUARD_BASELINE_WRITE=1`); a normal run is read-only and fails (never skips) when a dump is missing.

Restoring a fixture uses Legacy070Schema and raw inserts only — never production StorageSchema, migrations or models — because P3 changes them; the test proves Legacy070Schema DDL equals the production 0.7.0 DDL captured by DdlSnapshot::table on the same driver.

Deterministic data: fixed ULIDs and correlation ids, UTC second timestamps, rows ordered by primary key; driver-specific value normalisation (booleans, JSON text, datetime format) is explicit in one function and documented in the dump header.

The audit_log shape is compared in full (columns, types, nullability, unique event_id, secondary indexes, tenant pair constraint or SQLite triggers, host-key column types); hasTable alone is not evidence.
Every driver runs the same test file; sqlite-only assertions use the existing `sqlite` group convention; no new CI job.
A behavior that looks wrong at 0.7.0 is recorded (plan log/finding), never fixed here.
guidance:
Build order:

1. Freeze DDL: copy the 0.7.0 table definitions out of `StorageSchema` into `Legacy070Schema` (namespace `AzGuard\Tests\Fixtures\Baseline070\Persistence`). Add a test that, per driver, creates storage via production `StorageSchema::create('default')` and via `Legacy070Schema`, captures both with `DdlSnapshot::table` for all seven tables and asserts equality. Once green at P1 the production half of that assertion is the only part allowed to change later (P3 turns it into a six-table comparison).
2. Dataset: write `Dataset::seed()` with the Audit plugin enabled on panel A, disabled on panel B, both on the default storage; use the public grant/revoke/sync/touch and `azguard:grants:prune` paths so audit rows and revisions are produced by real code.
3. Writer: for each scenario, prepare the storage the way an installed 0.7.0 app would (loaded migrations / generated named migration / published copies then `migrate` / schema-1 shape then seed then `upgrade`), seed, then dump every AzGuard table and the AzGuard rows of `migrations` to `<driver>/<scenario>.json`.
4. Reader test: restore with `Restorer`, assert DDL (Legacy070Schema vs `tests/Fixtures/Storage/ddl/<driver>.json` for the shared tables), audit_log full shape, row equality with the dump, `verifySchema()` green on the current code, and the migrations-table basenames.

Local driver services: `docker compose up -d postgres mysql mariadb` (credentials and ports are the TestCase defaults).
deliverables: Legacy070Schema, Dataset and Restorer under tests/Fixtures/Baseline070/Persistence
16 row dumps (4 drivers × default/named/published/schema1) generated from the unchanged 0.7.0 code

result.notes: Legacy070Schema (proved equal to production 0.7.0 DDL per driver), Dataset (crm with Audit + ops without tenants/Audit, public API, all 11 journaled types), Scenario/Writer/Restorer, 16 dumps (4 drivers x default/named/published/schema1), deterministic per driver. PopulatedDatabaseTest 5/5 on sqlite/pgsql/mysql/mariadb. Grok 4.7 review: 1 finding fixed, round 2 GREEN. Hard risk: persistence/data integrity (Review P1.6).
deviations: V6: composer analyse fails on the 2 pre-existing phpstan errors in unchanged packages/ (same as P1.2); lint:check passes
V3/V4 ran with PGSQL_PORT=55432 / MYSQL_PORT=53306 (local docker port mapping)
